notes: Verified against a throwaway postgres:17-alpine: the new test passes on HEAD and fails against main's query (purchase counted 3 metrics/1 goal instead of 1/0, purchase_completed counted 2 instead of 1), so it genuinely discriminates the fix.
Full internal/httpapi suite passes on HEAD (356s) with the DB; no regressions in the catalog/MCP/analytical-guard tests.

jsonb_path_exists in default lax mode: '$.**' visits root and all descendants, '.event_name' on non-object values yields empty without error, and $name is bound via jsonb_build_object so the comparison is exact string equality. Requires PG12+; project uses PG17 in compose/CI.

Coverage gap, not a regression: a derived metric that references another metric by 'metric' name is not counted as using that metric's event (transitively). The old LIKE did not count it either unless the metric's name happened to contain the event name.

Coverage gap, not a regression: a filter object with property 'event_name' would not be matched since the path only looks at keys literally named event_name; the old text LIKE would have matched it by accident. Filters are compiled against properties, so this is unlikely to be a real usage pattern.
Diff is tightly scoped: 2-line SQL change plus a comment and one integration test; no migrations, auth, or external state touched; trivially revertable.
